about: The notebook's terms, as an encyclopedia links its words: each with the names it goes by, the page (and section) that explains it, and a line that says what it is, shown when the pointer rests on a link to it. book_fill links the first use of every term on every page (book_fill.link_terms) and lists them all on the glossary page. A name in lower case matches with either case of its first letter, one with capitals only as written; plurals match too. `skip` names, page by page, the terms a page uses in another sense.

terms.name: token
terms.says: The one thing of value in a world: every agent holds a whole number of them, and their total never changes.

terms.name: agent
terms.says: One member of a world: it lives on a node of the network, holds tokens and has a brain that takes all its decisions.

terms.name: connection
terms.says: A link between two agents of the network: they are neighbours, and can stake on each other's nodes.

terms.name: neighbour
terms.says: An agent joined to another by a connection.

terms.name: founder
terms.says: One of the agents a world starts with, each holding the same tokens, on a ring with a few shortcuts.

terms.name: iteration
terms.says: One step of a world's time: a phase of reproduction, then a phase of the game.

terms.name: game
terms.says: The second phase of an iteration: every agent stakes all its tokens on its own node and its neighbours', and every node goes to someone.

terms.name: candidate
terms.says: An agent itself and each of its neighbours, the ones its brain looks at when it decides.

terms.name: cleanup
terms.says: The end of every phase: only the largest connected piece of the network lives on, and the tokens of the dead are shared out.

terms.name: hegemon
terms.says: The agent that made the largest single stake on a node; it wins the node unless a coalition outbids it.

terms.name: revolution
terms.says: A node taken by stakers who each marked part of their stake revolutionary and together staked more than the largest single stake.

terms.name: brain
terms.says: The neural network each agent decides with: inputs about itself and its neighbours, outputs that become its decisions.

terms.name: message
terms.says: Numbers an agent writes to itself and to each neighbour every phase, which their brains read.

terms.name: share function
terms.says: How a brain's two numbers become one share between 0 and 1: of tokens for a child, or of a stake marked revolutionary.

terms.name: yes-or-no decision
terms.says: A yes or no a brain gives from four numbers: how strongly it means yes and no, and whether the stronger always wins or chance decides in proportion.

terms.name: largest remainder
terms.says: How tokens are split into whole numbers: each gets the whole part of its share, and the tokens left over go to the largest fractions.

terms.name: mutation
terms.says: A random change to a brain, made with a set probability when it is copied, and in B1 also after every game: a changed brain is a new genotype.

terms.name: genotype
terms.says: The identity of a brain: a number that a copy keeps and a change replaces, and that remembers the genotype it came from.

terms.name: seed
terms.says: The number that fixes every random choice of a run: the same settings and the same seed make the same world.

terms.name: setting
terms.says: One number or switch of a run's rules, fixed before it starts.

terms.name: extinction
terms.says: A world's end before its last iteration: it has dropped to its threshold of agents or fewer.

terms.name: lifetime
terms.says: How many iterations an agent lives, from its birth to its death.

terms.name: B1
terms.says: The first baseline: the algorithm exactly as a new run is offered it.

terms.name: B2
terms.says: The second baseline: B1 with the rules that keep its network from breaking and its agents from staking or breeding themselves to death.

terms.name: baseline
terms.says: The stated rules an experiment starts from and changes one thing of: B1 or B2.

terms.name: health bar
terms.says: The seven marks a world's network must meet to count as healthy: one piece, mostly on loops, no fatal cut, no hub, three to twelve links per agent, a dimension of 2.3 to 4.

terms.name: diversity score
terms.says: How much the agents of a world differ, in one number from 0 to 1: in tokens, links, ages and genotypes.

terms.name: effective kinds of staking
terms.says: How many different ways of staking a world's brains have, when all are put in the same situations, counted by how many agents use each.

terms.name: random twin
terms.says: A network with the same agents and as many links each, wired at random: what a world would be if it were no space at all.

terms.name: even split
terms.says: What the rules do when a brain scores no candidate above zero: the stake is spread evenly.

terms.name: estate
terms.says: The tokens a dead agent leaves, and who gets them.

terms.name: hub
terms.says: An agent joined to far more agents than most; a star is a world held together by a single hub.

terms.name: lab
terms.says: The program that runs an experiment's plan as runs, each on a frozen copy of the engine, the code that plays a world.

terms.name: pilot
terms.says: A world made by hand to see whether an idea is worth an experiment, without a thesis or many seeds.

terms.name: cross-time tournament
terms.says: Brains of a world at two moments, its eras, played against each other: do the later ones win?

terms.name: invasion test
terms.says: A strategy planted as a patch in an evolved world: does it spread, or die out?

terms.name: exploitability
terms.says: How much better than a world's brains the best reply to them would do: zero only at the top.

terms.name: open-ended evolution
terms.says: Evolution that keeps producing new things without end, not only up to a plateau.

terms.name: healthy world
terms.says: A world that meets all six criteria of the screen of random worlds; an interesting one is alive and misses only a few (at most two, provisionally, from round 3).

terms.name: half-cut exponent
terms.says: How the links crossing the cheapest cut of a world into halves grow with its size: 2/3 for a space of three dimensions, near 0 for a bottleneck, near 1 for a folded world.

terms.name: same-position share
terms.says: Of two agents put in the same situation, how often they stake their tokens measurably differently.

terms.name: Gini coefficient
terms.says: How unequally tokens are held: 0 if every agent holds as many, near 1 if one holds nearly all.

terms.name: richest tenth
terms.says: The share of all tokens held by the richest tenth of the agents.

terms.name: entropy
terms.says: How evenly something is shared out among the agents, from all in one place to spread perfectly evenly.

terms.name: share-out
terms.says: How a cleanup deals the tokens of the dead out among the living: in the baseline, each token to a survivor drawn at random.

terms.name: home stake
terms.says: The tokens an agent stakes on its own node, to keep it.

terms.name: degree
terms.says: The number of an agent's connections: how many neighbours it has.

terms.name: preferential attachment
terms.says: The well connected gaining new connections faster than the poorly connected.

terms.name: clustering
terms.says: How often an agent's neighbours are also each other's neighbours.

terms.name: path length
terms.says: How many connections the shortest way between two agents crosses.

terms.name: 2-core
terms.says: What is left of a network when agents with one connection or none are peeled away again and again: the agents on loops or between them.

terms.name: bridge
terms.says: A connection that lies on no loop: cut it and the network falls into two pieces.

terms.name: loop
terms.says: A path through the network that comes back to where it started without using a connection twice.

terms.name: cut risk
terms.says: The largest share of a world that cutting one connection would cut off.

terms.name: diameter
terms.says: The longest of the shortest paths between two agents of a world.

terms.name: spectral gap
terms.says: How hard a network is to cut into two halves, and how fast a walker on it forgets where it began.

terms.name: dimension
terms.says: How fast the number of agents within a distance grows with the distance: as its square in a plane, its cube in space.

terms.name: spectral dimension
terms.says: A network's dimension read from how a random walker spreads over it.

terms.name: box dimension
terms.says: A network's dimension read from how many boxes of a given size it takes to cover it.

terms.name: scaling relation
terms.says: How one property of an agent grows with another, as a power.

terms.name: assortativity
terms.says: Whether agents tend to be joined to agents like them: the well connected to the well connected.

terms.name: correlation length
terms.says: How far apart two agents can be and still be alike: how fast likeness fades with distance.

terms.name: token flow
terms.says: The tokens a game moves along each connection, from the agent who stakes to the node staked on.

terms.name: lightning
terms.says: A closed loop of the flow of a game: tokens that go round and come back where they started.

terms.name: token curvature
terms.says: How much richer an agent's neighbourhood is than the agent itself.

terms.name: circulation
terms.says: The part of a flow that goes round in loops, as against the part that runs from sources to sinks.

terms.name: flow module
terms.says: A group of agents that a token, following the flow, tends to stay inside.

terms.name: lineage
terms.says: A line of descent: the agents whose genotypes go back to one ancestor.

terms.name: common ancestor
terms.says: The genotype every living agent descends from, and how far back it lies.

terms.name: brain diversity
terms.says: How many different brains, or genotypes, a world holds.

terms.name: frame
terms.says: A whole world as a run records it after one phase: every agent, its tokens and connections.

terms.name: settled life
terms.says: A world from iteration 500 to its end, after its youth, where it is measured.

terms.name: median
terms.says: The middle value: half of the numbers lie below it and half above.

terms.name: correlation
terms.says: Whether two quantities go up and down together, from −1 to 1.

terms.name: autocorrelation
terms.says: How much a world's value now still says about its value some iterations later.

terms.name: mobility
terms.says: Whether the rich stay rich, or who holds the wealth keeps changing.

terms.name: participation ratio
terms.says: How many directions a cloud of points really uses.

terms.name: survival curve
terms.says: The share of lives that last at least so long, counted fairly when some are cut short by the end of a run.

terms.name: bootstrap
terms.says: How sure a number is, found by redrawing the worlds it came from many times.

terms.name: permutation test
terms.says: Whether a difference could be chance, found by shuffling which world belongs to which condition.

terms.name: Wilson interval
terms.says: The range a share probably lies in, when it was counted in only a few worlds.

terms.name: logarithmic axis
terms.says: An axis on which each step multiplies by the same factor, so that numbers of very different sizes fit on one chart.

terms.name: Muller plot
terms.says: A chart of how lines of descent grow, shrink and replace each other over time.

terms.name: least squares
terms.says: The straight line that fits a cloud of points best, and how much of their spread it explains.

terms.name: power law
terms.says: A quantity whose frequency falls as a power of its size: few huge values, many small ones.

terms.name: data collapse
terms.says: Curves of one quantity measured at many sizes that fall onto one another once its values are divided by a power of the size: then the size of the whole is its only scale.

terms.name: power spectrum
terms.says: How much of a series' wandering comes at each speed, from slow to fast.

terms.name: effective number
terms.says: How many kinds there really are, when kinds are counted by how much of the population they hold.

terms.name: fractional factorial
terms.says: A design that tests many switches together in few worlds, so that each one's effect can still be told apart.

terms.name: false discovery rate
terms.says: Among many tests at once, how often a result as strong as this one would be a false alarm (the rule of Benjamini and Hochberg).

terms.name: heredity index
terms.says: How much more a child acts like its parent than like a stranger, in the same situations: 1 as its parent does, 0 as a stranger does.

terms.name: effective population
terms.says: The size of a population left to chance that would lose its lines as fast: the smaller it is, the more chance decides which line survives.

terms.name: assembly theory
terms.says: A way to measure how much making went into a thing: the fewest steps that build it from basic parts, and how many copies of it there are.

terms.name: assembly index
terms.says: The fewest joins that build an object from basic blocks, when anything built before can be used again.

terms.name: addition chain
terms.says: Numbers from 1 in which each is the sum of two before it; the shortest one ending at m is the fewest joins m links can need.

terms.name: copy number
terms.says: How many identical copies of an object a collection holds.

terms.name: assembly
terms.says: Assembly theory's measure of a collection: each kind of object weighed by e to the power of its assembly index, times its copies beyond the first, over all the objects.

terms.name: ego network
terms.says: An agent, its neighbours and the links among them: the network as one agent sees it.
